mindfulness_exercises.title: Breathing Retraining (10:45)
mindfulness_exercises.description: Breathing Retraining is a technique for reducing your level of anxiety. It is a simple technique that can be used anywhere and at any time.

mindfulness_exercises.title: Body Scan Meditation (4:01)
mindfulness_exercises.description: Body Scan Meditation is a type of mindfulness meditation that involves bringing awareness to different parts of the body and noticing physical sensations without judgment.

mindfulness_exercises.title: Mountain Meditation (8:12)
mindfulness_exercises.description: Mountain Meditation is a type of guided imagery meditation that involves visualizing yourself as a mountain, steady and strong, while observing your thoughts and feelings as clouds passing by.

mindfulness_exercises.title: Rain and Thunder Sounds (9:37)
mindfulness_exercises.description: The sound of rain can lower your anxiety levels, promote relaxation and enhance the quality of sleep.

mindfulness_exercises.title: Mood Doodle (5 min)
mindfulness_exercises.description: A simple drawing exercise to express how you're feeling without needing any words or artistic skill.
steps: Grab any paper and pen you have nearby
Set a timer for 5 minutes
Draw your current mood using only lines, shapes, or scribbles - it doesn't need to look like anything
Look at what you drew, then let it go - there's nothing to judge here

mindfulness_exercises.title: Color Your Mood (15 min)
mindfulness_exercises.description: A painting exercise using color to process emotion, with no pressure to create something 'good'.
steps: Use any paints, markers, or crayons you have on hand
Pick colors that match how you're feeling right now
Fill a page freely for about 15 minutes, no plan needed
Notice how you feel afterward compared to before you started

mindfulness_exercises.title: Free Movement Break (5 min)
mindfulness_exercises.description: A short movement and dancing break to release built-up physical tension and shift your mood.
steps: Put on any song you like, or just move in silence
Stand up and gently shake out your arms and shoulders
Let your body move however feels natural for the length of one song
No steps to get right - the only goal is to move

mindfulness_exercises.title: Quick Activity Boost (10 min)
mindfulness_exercises.description: A short burst of physical activity to release tension and boost mood through movement.
steps: Pick any physical activity you enjoy - a walk, stretching, shooting hoops, a quick sport
Set a light goal of just 10 minutes, no pressure to do more
Notice your breathing and body as you move, rather than rushing through it
Afterward, take a moment to notice how your energy or mood has shifted

mindfulness_exercises.title: 4-7-8 Breathing for Sleep (3 min)
mindfulness_exercises.description: A simple breathing pattern that helps slow your heart rate and signal to your body that it's time to sleep.
steps: Lie down comfortably and close your eyes
Breathe in quietly through your nose for 4 seconds
Hold your breath for 7 seconds
Exhale slowly through your mouth for 8 seconds, making a soft whoosh sound
Repeat this cycle 4 times, letting your body relax more with each round

mindfulness_exercises.title: Progressive Muscle Relaxation (8 min)
mindfulness_exercises.description: A technique for releasing physical tension by tensing and relaxing each muscle group in turn, helping your body settle before sleep.
steps: Lie down and take a few slow breaths to settle in
Starting with your feet, tense the muscles tightly for 5 seconds, then release completely
Move up to your calves, then thighs - tense for 5 seconds, then let go
Continue up through your stomach, hands, arms, shoulders, and finally your face
After finishing, lie still for a minute and notice the heaviness and relaxation in your body

mindfulness_exercises.title: Wind-Down Routine Checklist (5 min)
mindfulness_exercises.description: A short pre-bed checklist to signal to your body and mind that it's time to sleep.
steps: Dim the lights in your room, or switch to a warm lamp instead of overhead light
Put your phone somewhere out of arm's reach, ideally outside the bedroom
Take 5 slow, deep breaths, making each exhale a little longer than the last
Gently stretch your neck and shoulders for 30 seconds
Write or think of one small thing you're looking forward to tomorrow

mindfulness_exercises.title: Worry Dump Before Bed (5 min)
mindfulness_exercises.description: A quick writing exercise to get racing thoughts out of your head and onto paper, so they're less likely to keep you awake.
steps: Grab any notebook or piece of paper - this isn't for anyone else to read
Set a timer for 5 minutes
Write down everything on your mind right now, without worrying about order or grammar
When the timer ends, close the notebook - you can return to these thoughts tomorrow if needed
Take a few slow breaths before settling in to sleep
